content:
In June this year, we pointed out three cases where Russian banks sanctioned by the United States bypassed review and put their client applications on the App Store. Two months later, another example has reached the top of the iPhone App Store.

K8CHEN PRO is the latest case. The App Store listing disguises it as an augmented reality (AR)-driven kitchen design application.

Once the app is opened, the disguise almost immediately disappears. The privacy policy linked from the App Store is marked as generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator," which in itself may be a warning sign.

Regardless, the app is undoubtedly T-Bank's client application. What I find interesting is that such apps can repeatedly pass the App Store review process.

When they are widely reported and climb the App Store charts, it is plainly obvious that they are not the kind of apps that should appear there. The situation is thought-provoking.

The other two cases mentioned in June can be found here and here.

Update: Predictably, the app has already been removed from the App Store.

Make the most of your Apple products
